name: BTC observable level-two liquidity shock
description: Compares current combined observable five-basis-point base depth and mean venue spread in basis points with the arithmetic mean of the prior 60 valid one-second book observations. The Kraken input is pinned to its top-100-level subscription. depth_ratio_60s and spread_ratio_60s expose the continuous change. State is shock when depth is at or below 0.50 of baseline or spread is at or above 2.0 times baseline; thinning below 0.75 depth or above 1.5 spread; recovering when the immediately prior state was shock and the current observation has left shock but remains thinning; otherwise normal. The 0.50, 0.75, 1.5, and 2.0 classification boundaries are initial research thresholds that require empirical calibration. Missing, non-ready, or non-contiguous one-second book observations break continuity and restart warm-up. This level-two signal measures observable thinning and widening; it does not attribute a change to cancellation or execution. Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
